name: guard-deletion
description: trigger: a change that removes a check, auth decorator, middleware registration, sanitizer call or path check with none of its kind in the same hunk (ask), or removes a hardening flag, security header, cookie attribute, TLS check or row-level security, or swaps one of those or a narrow file mode for a weakened form (block). Hunk-local: misses a guard moved across hunks or files, one neutralised in place, added insecure settings, a deletion-only commit. [Session-enforced via PreToolUse and Stop hooks; needs git and a Python 3.11+. PreToolUse judges the file a tool call would write; Stop re-reads what the turn actually left on disk, so a file written through a shell heredoc is judged too. With no working Python the hook exits 2; without git, fail-open clients allow silently. A gate that cannot reach a decision refuses rather than allowing one it never judged. Enforcement at every commit and in CI still needs chock installed in the repo. Codex requires a one-time trust review per hook -- the plugin is ADVISORY until you approve its hook, and a plugin update voids that trust until re-approved.]
